trajectory_summary: This is a smooth, cooperative call that ends in a booked appointment with the bill-text sent and confirmed live. The rep executes verify items in order, holds scope correctly on pricing questions, and locks a date/time — but leaves several value-building opportunities (bill-pain acknowledgment, tree-removal enthusiasm, repeated cost curiosity) unaddressed, and the co-owner/title question is muddled by a likely mis-transcription.

observed_outcome.quote: Got you down for, Wednesday next Wednesday, the, twenty ninth at 10:30. And, yeah, we'll see you then.
observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day (Wednesday the 29th) and time (10:30) are confirmed verbally by the rep and not disputed by the customer, meeting the booked threshold. However, the confirmed co-owner from 02:13 is never named or invited to the appointment, so co_owner_confirmed is false despite the appointment being locked.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The rep captured the bill figure and even had the customer flag it as rising ('that that will go up') but responded only with 'Right. Okay. So it's going up. Gotcha. Okay.' — acknowledgment without turning it into urgency or emotional alignment against the utility.

bill_document_audit.ask_quote: Do you typically get those in the mail or online?
bill_document_audit.result_quote: Were you able to receive that text message? Just wanna make sure you you have it. I got a text, and I'm getting a second. Oh, yes. I was able to get that text.
bill_document_audit.reasoning: The rep sent a text link and confirmed the customer received the text itself, but the actual bill photo was not sent or received by the end of the call — the appointment is booked pending the customer sending the photo afterward, so this is promised_later rather than received_on_call.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep never explicitly asks 'what got you interested in solar' — the call moves from address/homeowner verification directly into roof and program details without a dedicated interest-motivation question, so no reason was captured to reinforce later.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: co-owner not identified or invited to appointment
primary_coaching_focus.quote: There is. And anyone who makes the decisions.
primary_coaching_focus.why: Customer clearly confirms a co-owner/decision-maker exists on the title, and the rep never follows up to get a name or invite them to Wednesday's appointment — this is the single highest-leverage gap on the call per protocols.spouse_decision, and it structurally weakens the booked appointment.

key_moments.quote: It is a single family home. We do have a couple of trees. We we do have some and I am happy to take them out or part of them or cut them way back
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer proactively volunteers to remove trees to improve solar viability — a strong buying signal showing she's already problem-solving toward a system, not just curious.

key_moments.quote: There is. And anyone who makes the decisions.
key_moments.stewart_read: The customer confirms there is a co-owner on the title who is also a decision-maker. This is a direct, unambiguous affirmative to the rep's co-owner question and triggers the spouse/co-owner inclusion protocol — the rep never asks who this person is or attempts to include them on the appointment.

key_moments.quote: Okay. No worries. If I surprise it, we can go ahead.
key_moments.stewart_read: This follow-on line is garbled by the transcription but reads as the customer suggesting she can proceed and surprise the co-owner/decision-maker rather than requiring their attendance — it does not resolve whether the co-owner will actually be present, it just signals the customer's own workaround. It does not substitute for the rep confirming co-owner attendance per protocol.

key_moments.quote: Yeah. So that's something a specialist can kinda go over with you once we get that design put together.
key_moments.stewart_read: This is a clean, correct execution of the universal escape hatch — the rep does not guess at savings numbers and redirects to the specialist appropriately.
